content:
SELECTED_INDEX: 10
CONFIDENCE: 0.22
EXPLANATION: The dominant Raman band at 1778 cm⁻¹ indicates a highly strained cyclic C=O (typical of five-membered lactones/peroxides, ν(C=O) 1760–1790 cm⁻¹).  Additional medium bands at 1256 cm⁻¹ and 952 cm⁻¹ are characteristic of O–O related vibrations (δ(OO) ≈ 1260 cm⁻¹, ν(OO) ≈ 900–1000 cm⁻¹, cf. rule GFQ-069 for H₂O₂).  The 818 cm⁻¹ peak fits an O–O–C ring stretching mode often seen for cyclic peroxides.  Candidate 10 (O=C1CCOOO1) is the only structure that contains an O–O (indeed O–O–O) linkage together with a strained lactone carbonyl, matching the key 952/1256/1778 cm⁻¹ triplet.  None of the other candidates possess O–O bonds, making them less consistent with these diagnostic peaks.
